title: Show HN: Socratui – A Socratic Tutor for the Terminal
text:
Hi all!

I am really enjoying using the [socratic tutor skill by Jane Street](https://github.com/janestreet/agent_skills/blob/master/socra...), and I'm hoping to build a sticky learning routine around it, but don't really like the UX of using it inside Claude Code; so I built this dedicated tui for it, which also adds flashcard reviews, anki cards exports, and other nice features.

Hope you enjoy it!

Comments, criticisms and PRs welcome :)

title: Re: Microsoft Status: "We are re-routing the protocols...
text:
Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services

Issue ID: MO1550821 Affected services: Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 suite, Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365), Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online Status: Service degradation Issue type: Incident

User impact Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services.

More info More info: Potentially impacted services include: - Exchange Online - Microsoft Teams - SharePoint Online - Microsoft Copilot 365 - Microsoft Defender XDR - Microsoft Planner - Microsoft To Do - Microsoft Purview: Multiple Purview services including Authorization, Auto Labelling, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Communication Compliance, and Data Classification are impacted.

Scope of impact This issue may affect users attempting to access the affected Microsoft 365 services.

Current status We've validated an alternative health check method on a subset of affected infrastructure, which allowed the servers in that subset to successfully return to service, and we're now applying this change more broadly. We're also preparing an automated recovery process to continually detect and restart unresponsive servers, to help keep them in service while this change progresses. Additionally, our review of recent changes has identified a small number of configuration updates that we're investigating as potential contributors to the issue.

History of updates

- While we haven't identified any recent changes that correlate with the start of impact, our investigation indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component on the affected servers that's responsible for processing them. We're deploying a targeted change to bypass this component on a subset of servers to validate whether this restores availability, and we've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being removed from service while we work to return the affected servers to service. We're also investigating why affected servers are experiencing elevated processor usage while handling requests.

- We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact. As a precaution, we've paused all deployments and configuration changes while we review recent changes for any correlation to this event. We've determined that the elevated load isn't driven by an overall increase in traffic, but by a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable, which is shifting load onto the remaining infrastructure. We're investigating what's causing these servers to become unavailable while we work to safely return them to service.

- We've completed redistributing connection traffic across our worldwide infrastructure, and we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure to further reduce load. We're also restarting affected servers to return them to service. In parallel, we're investigating whether the elevated traffic reflects a genuine increase in requests or a shift in how traffic is being routed across our infrastructure.

- We’re investigating an issue impacting multiple Microsoft 365 services and we've determined the affected infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors. We're restarting and repairing impacted portions of this infrastructure to restore capacity, and reviewing an unexpected increase in a specific type of service traffic to determine whether it's contributing to the elevated load. In parallel, we're evaluating options to redirect traffic to alternate infrastructure to expedite relief.

title: Re: Vibes Don't Maintain...
text:
> "...or the parts that have never once executed in production because they’re there for a worst case someone sat down and imagined."

Good stuff.

> "It’s the record of what the code was supposed to do ... written down somewhere a human or an agent can read them back. Ours are markdown files in git..."

I keep getting surprised how many quite technical people I know are doing real work with AI but have never touched markdown.

If you are one of those people, allow me to offer a suggestion:

Stop. No more sending questions to ChatGPT or Claude until you do the following:

- Install Typora on your Windows or Mac machine.

- Write a .md (markdown text) file a full page long using Typora (or another editor that understands markdown, but Typora will do just fine). Make use of Heading 1, Heading 2, and underline formatting, at least.

- Make the one page file be a complex request to an AI. Something like "research x, compare it to y, make a guess what will happen in the future, here are some of my opinions and guesses, make your replies short, provide references".

Hand that .md file to your favorite AI. (Bonus points for using drag and drop or pointing the AI at the dir the file is in.) Look at your results. Make a change to your .md file. Hand it to the AI again, see the different results.

In my opinion, if you work on a keyboard and you've been making use of AI for the last 8 months, you should have done the above 4 months ago. Until you do, you will have a hard time understanding how drastically AI has changed almost all developer's lives, and how it is changing more and more fields that are not software development.

title: Re: Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Orchestrator...
text:
This is essentially what Anthropic does with the advisor mode and what GitHub does with their multi-model pipeline using the HydraFusion model, which is just a large set of different models with different qualities used in a pipeline to produce an answer.

What I don't understand is how they all make it work with caching in general. Looking at how the advisor mode in claude work you seem to only be billed the output tokens and cache hit on the whole session when it calls out to the advisor, making it super cheap compared to running the more expensive model for the entire session.

title: Show HN: DeployAngel – A verdict in ~20 minutes if a deploy broke production
text:
Hey there, I'm looking for feedback on a release verification tool I'm building.

https://www.deployangel.com

I decided to build this after an issue popped up with a recent Rails upgrade. We upgraded a Rails app to 8.1 and picked up a new default that changes the order after_commit callbacks run. Our upload code started telling the virus scanner about files before they were saved to S3, and the scanner just quietly dropped them. No exceptions were raised and uploads sat in "processing" for days. We should have had alarms in place, we know that now but I wondered if there could be some type monitoring that would just have noticed the change. I did some checking and the callback route went from roughly 27 requests an hour to zero when we deployed. That seems like a fairly easy change in behavior to automatically raise an alarm. So after a few weekends working with Claude I have a new tool.

A small agent sends one aggregated payload per minute. Then the server compares each release with the last one it cleared. It looks at things like error rates, latency per route, traffic that collapses, and missing job runs. The server then returns a verdict if the release cleared or not. Currently I have agents for Rails, Django, FastAPI, and ASP.NET Core.

It will work best for teams that deploy often and the app gets steady traffic. It's not meant to replace error monitoring tools like Sentry, but to work alongside them. Here's a recent release of its own: https://app.deployangel.com/share/KAaurrfRHcw43ZrjkWst2DLY?r...

The agents are MIT-licensed. It's completely free right now, with a free tier planned.

https://github.com/DeployAngel

I'm looking for a few teams to run it on a real app for a couple of weeks. I'd love to hear if it surfaces issues that other monitoring and alarms miss. Of course I'm hoping it proves to be useful, but if not, that's good information too.
